root_cause: The datepicker does not hide on blur when the entered date is outside the allowed range, because the update/setDate logic early exits without hiding and no blur listener is registered to close the picker. Additionally, the input field is not updated with the last valid date on blur.
repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field that calls this.update() to refresh the input field with the last valid selection (or the typed date if valid) and this.hide() to ensure the datepicker closes regardless of validation outcome.
expected_accessibility_effect: Ensures keyboard users can navigate away from the date field using Tab and the datepicker calendar will close, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order). The input field will show a valid date.
functional_risks: Hiding the picker on blur may affect workflows where users expect the picker to remain open while interacting with other controls, but this aligns with typical datepicker behavior.
Calling update on blur may cause the selection to change if the typed date is valid, which is intended.
verification_requirements: After edit, typing a valid or invalid date and pressing Tab results in the datepicker closing (.datepicker not visible) and focus moving to the next element.
The input field displays a valid date (the typed date if valid, otherwise the previous valid date).
Selecting a date from the picker and then tabbing away also closes the picker.
All existing date selection and navigation functionality remains intact.
